<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Combine age at death, labelled answers, calendar periods and cause of death in one private table.
</div>

This chapter uses the 24-person synthetic questionnaire test fixture described in [Getting started](book-00-start.html).
**You need:** the packages and the matching practice connection described in
[Before you start](book-00-start.html#before-you-start).
Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed
with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.5. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Concept selections refer to the searches and saved definitions in
[chapter 4](book-04-vocabulary.html), including the separate questionnaire
catalogue. Additional body-measurement concepts are found on screen in the
[formula walkthrough](book-15-formulas.html#find-the-inputs-before-calculating).

## Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the `book-work` directory created in
[Getting started](book-00-start.html#get-the-book-helpers). Run this setup first:


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture()
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
```

```
#> [1] "site"
```

The `site` connection is ready. This chapter creates its temporary questionnaire fixture locally.

## Find the questionnaire concepts first

The local catalogue is the chapter-4 questionnaire vocabulary, not GiBleed's
clinical vocabulary. Search before selecting questions and coded answers.


``` r
va_catalogue <- ds.omop.concept.search(NULL, standard_only = FALSE, limit = 100, conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(va_catalogue[c("concept_name", "domain_id", "standard_concept")])
```



|concept_name          |domain_id   |standard_concept |
|:---------------------|:-----------|:----------------|
|Education question    |Observation |S                |
|Fever question        |Observation |S                |
|Secondary education   |Meas Value  |S                |
|University education  |Meas Value  |S                |
|Myocardial infarction |Condition   |S                |
|Pneumonia             |Condition   |S                |
|Yes                   |Meas Value  |S                |
|No                    |Meas Value  |S                |
|Inpatient Visit       |Meas Value  |S                |
|Outpatient Visit      |Meas Value  |S                |
|Education answer      |Meas Value  |S                |
|Practice medicine     |Drug        |S                |
|Practice measurement  |Measurement |S                |
|kilogram              |Unit        |S                |

``` r
va_ids <- setNames(va_catalogue$concept_id, va_catalogue$concept_name)
va_sets <- lapply(va_ids, omop_concept_set)
```

These local concepts have no external Maps to or ancestry. Their observed uses
were checked in [chapter 4](book-04-vocabulary.html#find-the-colleagues-questions-answers-and-causes).

## Begin with the clinical question

We want one row per person, including people with missing information. Each row
will contain a pseudonymous `person_id`, completed age at death, education and fever
answers, first-visit calendar periods and cause of death. The analyst sees only
summaries of those columns.

“Latest answer” here means the latest nonmissing answer to each question across
all available history. It is **not** automatically restricted to before death or
to the first visit. Define those restrictions explicitly for your actual study.

## Keep the question separate from its answer


``` r
education <- omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", concepts = 900001L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"))
class(education)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"
```

This is the same education definition as chapter 5. Reusing it keeps one
categorical column with vocabulary names.


``` r
fever <- omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", concepts = 900002L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"))
class(fever)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"
```

The second question gets its own column. This capstone uses vocabulary labels
`Yes` and `No`; chapter 5 demonstrated a user-defined lower-case recode.

## Compute completed age at death


``` r
age_at_death <- omop_age_at("death")
class(age_at_death)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"
```

The default unit is completed years, using the full birth date and death date.
It is not simply death year minus birth year. With the default partial-date policy,
an incomplete birth date produces missing age; missing death also produces missing age.
No January 1 birthday is silently invented.

## Select the first visit once


``` r
first_visit <- omop_anchor(omop_event("visit_occurrence"), which = "first")
class(first_visit)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_anchor" "list"
```

All calendar presentations below refer to this same first visit. An anchor is a
selection rule; it is not a patient date returned to your R session.

## Present its month


``` r
visit_month <- omop_date(first_visit, omop_date_spec(precision = "month"))
class(visit_month)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"
```

The values will be ordered categories such as year-month. No manual date-string
mutation or fixed 64-boundary cut vector is needed in 2.10.5.

## Present its quarter and year


``` r
visit_quarter <- omop_date(first_visit, omop_date_spec(precision = "quarter"))
visit_year <- omop_date(first_visit,
  omop_date_spec(precision = "year", representation = "number"))
class(visit_quarter)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"
```

Quarter labels distinguish both year and quarter. The numeric year variant is
included to match the released native colleague recipe exactly. Precision is
chosen separately for each variable.

## Add the coded cause


``` r
cause <- omop_variable(event = omop_event("death"),
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", value = "cause_concept_id"))
class(cause)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"
```

The vocabulary supplies the label. People without death records keep missing
cause and age, while remaining in the all-person output.

## Assemble the released native recipe

The following completes the exact variable set in the released follow-up
`tools/dates/va-native.R`, which closed the earlier feasibility gaps. It also
includes age at first visit, exact visit/death dates and separate visit date parts
so you can distinguish those types. Every one of these values stays on the server.


``` r
death <- omop_anchor(omop_event("death"), which = "first")
va <- omop_recipe(variables = list(
  age_at_death = age_at_death, age_at_first_visit = omop_age_at("first_visit"),
  education = education, fever = fever,
  visit_date = omop_date(first_visit), visit_month = visit_month,
  visit_quarter = visit_quarter, visit_year = visit_year,
  visit_parts = omop_date_parts(first_visit, c("year", "month")),
  death_date = omop_date(death), cause_of_death = cause),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"),
  options = list(translate_concepts = TRUE))
class(va)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_recipe" "list"
```

For a smaller analysis table, select only the variables your question needs using
`columns` in `omop_output()`. The full version here is the regression-tested
colleague recipe, rather than the old feasibility workaround.

## Explain and assign


``` r
explanation <- recipe_explain(va, conns = conns)
stopifnot(explanation$selected == "v2")
explanation$selected
```

```
#> [1] "v2"
```


``` r
print(recipe_execute(va, out = c(people = "D_va"), conns = conns))
```

```
#> people 
#> "D_va"
```

A successful symbol mapping means the server assigned the private wide table.
It does not mean that a local object named `D_va` now holds patient rows.

## Inspect column names


``` r
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_va", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#>  [1] "person_id"          "age_at_death"       "age_at_first_visit" "education"         
#>  [5] "fever"              "visit_date"         "visit_month"        "visit_quarter"     
#>  [9] "visit_year"         "visit_parts_year"   "visit_parts_month"  "death_date"        
#> [13] "cause_of_death"
```

The column list includes `person_id`. Its server values are pseudonyms. We do
not print them or use them as local merge keys.

## Summarise completed age


``` r
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_va$age_at_death", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean 
#>   33   33   33   38   43   43   43   38
```

In the synthetic patterns, supported complete birth dates give completed ages
33 and 43. The other patterns have incomplete birth or no death, so their ages
are missing. The displayed summary is the actual aggregate returned by dsBase.

## Show education and fever


``` r
ds.omop.table("D_va", "education", conns = conns)
```

```
#> D_va$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6
```

Each education category represents an answer, not a separate column.


``` r
ds.omop.table("D_va", "fever", conns = conns)
```

```
#> D_va$fever
#> Yes  No 
#>   6   6
```

Missing responses are excluded from these counts. “No” is an observed answer,
not an imputation for missingness.

## Show the calendar periods


``` r
ds.omop.table("D_va", "visit_month", conns = conns)
```

```
#> D_va$visit_month
#> 2020-03 2020-06 2020-07 
#>       6       6       6
```

These month counts group people by their first visit.


``` r
ds.omop.table("D_va", "visit_quarter", conns = conns)
```

```
#> D_va$visit_quarter
#> 2020-Q1 2020-Q2 2020-Q3 
#>       6       6       6
```

Several months can belong to one quarter; the grouped counts reflect that.

## Show the cause categories


``` r
ds.omop.table("D_va", "cause_of_death", conns = conns)
```

```
#> D_va$cause_of_death
#> Myocardial infarction             Pneumonia 
#>                    12                     6
```

All shown category tables contain labels, never numeric concept IDs. The recipe
produces person rows privately; the book deliberately shows aggregates rather than
a row preview, even though the development fixture is synthetic.

## Exercise 2: a common variant

Count education in the completed verbal-autopsy table.

<details><summary>Solution 2</summary>


``` r
ds.omop.table("D_va", "education", conns = conns)
```

```
#> D_va$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6
```

This is one categorical answer per person, not one binary column for each answer.

</details>

## Exercise 3: a pitfall to avoid

Inspect the final table schema without downloading the table.

<details><summary>Solution 3</summary>


``` r
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_va", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#>  [1] "person_id"          "age_at_death"       "age_at_first_visit" "education"         
#>  [5] "fever"              "visit_date"         "visit_month"        "visit_quarter"     
#>  [9] "visit_year"         "visit_parts_year"   "visit_parts_month"  "death_date"        
#> [13] "cause_of_death"
```

Its private columns combine several domains. The approved aggregate remains the analyst-facing result.

</details>
## Add a native numeric presentation

Keep exact completed age private and add a broad age band with the A-29 numeric
wrapper. Missing age stays missing. These public teaching bands do not repair
incomplete birth dates or infer an age for a survivor.


``` r
va_numeric <- omop_recipe(variables = c(va$variables,
  list(age_band = omop_number_bins(age_at_death, breaks = c(0, 40, 121),
    labels = c("under 40", "40 and over")))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(va_numeric, out = c(people = "D_va_numeric"), conns = conns))
```

```
#>         people 
#> "D_va_numeric"
```

``` r
ds.omop.table("D_va_numeric", "age_band", conns = conns)
```

```
#> D_va_numeric$age_band
#>    under 40 40 and over 
#>           6           6
```

The earlier date presentation and concept translation remain native. Custom
category order, rollups, wide-by-time layout and codebooks await the separate
categorical/layout update; this chapter does not invent arguments for them.

## Recap

The native 2.10.5 API now supports the whole capstone: pseudonymous roster, completed age, coded answers, calendar periods and cause of death.
